entries.name: Apache OpenEJB
entries.definition: A lightweight container that implements the Enterprise JavaBeans (EJB) specification and can run standalone or embedded in another server.

entries.name: Apache OpenNLP
entries.definition: An Apache open-source machine-learning library for natural language processing tasks such as tokenisation, part-of-speech tagging and named-entity recognition.

entries.name: Apache PDFBox
entries.definition: An open-source Java library from the Apache Software Foundation for creating, reading, changing and extracting text from PDF files.

entries.name: Apache PredictionIO
entries.definition: An open-source machine-learning server for building and serving predictive engines, developed as an Apache Software Foundation project.

entries.name: Apache Spark
entries.definition: An open-source engine for large-scale data processing and analytics, with programming interfaces for Scala, Java, Python and R.

entries.name: API design
entries.definition: Designing the interface through which other programs use a service, including its resources, operations, data formats and errors.

entries.name: API gateway
entries.definition: A server that sits in front of backend services and routes, secures and manages the API requests that clients send to them.

entries.name: API management
entries.definition: Publishing, securing, monitoring and versioning APIs across their lifetime, often with an API gateway and a developer portal.

entries.name: Apollo GraphQL
entries.definition: Apollo's platform and open-source tools, such as Apollo Client and Apollo Server, for building, running and querying GraphQL APIs.

entries.name: Appian
entries.definition: A low-code platform for building business process, workflow and case management applications.

entries.name: Apple Device Enrollment Program
entries.definition: An Apple program, now called Automated Device Enrollment, that lets an organisation enrol company-owned Apple devices in its device-management system automatically when they are first switched on.

entries.name: Apple Numbers
entries.definition: Apple's spreadsheet application for macOS, iOS and iPadOS.

entries.name: appletviewer
entries.definition: A command-line tool in the Java Development Kit that runs Java applets without a web browser.

entries.name: Application controls
entries.definition: The checks built into a business application, automated or manual, that make sure transactions are processed completely, accurately and with proper authorisation, as examined in IT audit.

entries.name: Application delivery controller
entries.definition: A network device or service placed in front of application servers that balances traffic and adds features such as SSL offloading, caching and application firewalling.

entries.name: Application delivery network
entries.definition: A set of network technologies, such as load balancers and WAN optimisation, that together keep web applications fast, available and secure.

entries.name: Application monitoring
entries.definition: Tracking the availability, performance and errors of a running software application.

entries.name: Application pool
entries.definition: In Microsoft Internet Information Services (IIS), a group of web applications that share a worker process and settings and are isolated from applications in other pools.

entries.name: Application programming interface
entries.definition: A defined set of operations and data formats through which one piece of software lets other programs use its functions.

entries.name: Application-specific integrated circuit
entries.definition: An integrated circuit designed for one particular purpose or product rather than for general-purpose use.

entries.name: Applied element method
entries.definition: A numerical method in structural engineering that models a structure as small rigid elements joined by springs, so that its behaviour can be simulated up to collapse.

entries.name: Applied linguistics
entries.definition: The study of language-related problems in real-world settings, such as language teaching, translation and language policy.

entries.name: Applied statistics
entries.definition: The use of statistical methods to analyse data and solve practical problems in a particular field, as opposed to developing statistical theory.

entries.name: Applixware
entries.definition: An office productivity suite for Unix and Linux systems made by Applix.

entries.name: AppsFlyer
entries.definition: A platform for mobile attribution and marketing analytics that shows which campaigns lead to app installs and in-app activity.

entries.name: AppSheet
entries.definition: Google's no-code platform for building apps from data in spreadsheets and databases.

entries.name: Apptio
entries.definition: Software for technology business management that tracks, allocates and reports on the cost of IT.

entries.name: apxs
entries.definition: A command-line tool of the Apache HTTP Server for building and installing extension modules as dynamic shared objects.

entries.name: Arachnophilia
entries.definition: A free text editor for writing web pages and other code.

entries.name: ArangoDB
entries.definition: A multi-model database that stores documents, graphs and key-value data and is queried with its own language, AQL.

entries.name: Araxis Merge
entries.definition: A commercial tool for comparing and merging files, folders and documents, made by Araxis.

entries.name: Archaeology
entries.definition: The study of past human societies through the excavation and analysis of their material remains.

entries.name: Architectural rendering
entries.definition: Producing realistic images of a planned building or interior from a 3D design model.

entries.name: Architectural visualization
entries.definition: Producing images, animations or virtual walkthroughs that show how a planned building or space will look before it is built.

entries.name: ArcSight Enterprise Security Manager
entries.definition: A security information and event management (SIEM) product that collects and correlates security events from across an organisation to detect threats.

entries.name: Areca Backup
entries.definition: A free, open-source file backup application written in Java.

entries.name: Argo CD
entries.definition: A declarative GitOps continuous-delivery tool that keeps applications on Kubernetes in sync with configuration stored in Git.

entries.name: Arithmetic
entries.definition: The branch of mathematics that deals with calculating with numbers using addition, subtraction, multiplication and division.

entries.name: ARKit
entries.definition: Apple's framework for building augmented reality apps on iOS and iPadOS.

entries.name: Armed Forces Health Longitudinal Technology Application
entries.definition: The electronic health record system that the US Department of Defense used across its Military Health System to document patient care.
variants: Armed Forces Health Longitudinal Technology Application (AHTLA)
